review_output: {"summary":"No blocker. The window, cohort and 7-day inclusive-boundary logic matches the approved rules, and the proposal example and T-boundary tests check out by hand. Main risks: (1) completion has two sources of truth (coverage vs durable ingestion fact) with no reconciliation, and known-empty [] is treated as unknown; (2) floating-point media projection and T-1 truncation can misclassify exact-90%/T-boundary cases at non-unit rates; (3) validation is lazy and over-broad; (4) tests miss several boundaries. Not production-ready, which matches the stated no-production-use status.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","file":"live-core-metrics-read-model.ts","area":"completion/order consistency","issue":"Completion is derived from coverage, but order timing comes from separate durable facts that are never reconciled with it.","evidence":"orderMetrics only checks at >= verifiedAt and at < endMs for persons in `completed`. Durable completions for people not in `completed` are ignored; a durable time earlier than physically possible from that person's viewing is accepted. completions=[] (audited empty) with a coverage-completed person returns missing_data, same as null.","impact":"C and O/C can disagree silently; a known contradiction is reported as unknown history, violating the null vs [] rule.","recommended_fix":"Fail closed (invalid_data) when [] or a missing/conflicting durable time contradicts coverage-completed people, or a durable time precedes the earliest feasible crossing or follows the person's last wall time. Keep null as missing_data.","required_test":"completions=[] with a coverage-completed person → invalid_data; durable completion before feasible crossing → invalid_data; durable completion for a non-completed person → defined result.","confidence":0.75},{"severity":"MAJOR","file":"live-core-metrics-read-model.ts","area":"boundary precision","issue":"Media positions use floating-point rate multiplication, then ceil/floor, so exact-integer positions can drop 1 ms.","evidence":"rate = media/wall; floor(mediaStart + offset*rate). (a/b)*b is not always a, e.g. 1/49*49 = 0.9999999999999999 (wall 49000, media 1000 → 999). Measured ratios like 29970/30000 are plausible.","impact":"A person exactly at 90% coverage, or one whose threshold lands at T, can be misclassified; the 'inward rounding never invents coverage' comment hides spurious undercount.","recommended_fix":"Use exact integer/BigInt rational arithmetic: ceil/floor((mediaDelta*wallOffset)/wallLen) with no float rate.","required_test":"Property/table tests with non-binary rates (e.g. 29970/30000, 1000/49000) asserting integer endpoints unclipped and exact 90% boundary stays complete.","confidence":0.7},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"live-core-metrics-read-model.ts","area":"T boundary semantics","issue":"Using endMs-1 for media truncates at integer-ms wall positions, which is exact only for rate 1.","evidence":"end = floor(mediaStart + (min(T-1, wallEnd)-wallStart)*rate). At rate 2 a crossing at wall T-0.5 is strictly before T but position(T-1) is below threshold, so it is excluded. Wall exposure runs to T while coverage stops at T-1.","impact":"Completions in the final millisecond at non-unit rates are dropped; durable ingestion time rounding is undefined relative to this.","recommended_fix":"Define crossing time as the exact rational instant, convert to ms with a stated rounding rule shared with ingestion, and compare it to T.","required_test":"Rate 2 and 0.5 segments whose threshold crossing falls at T-1, T-0.5 and T; assert agreement with the durable timestamp convention.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"live-core-metrics-read-model.ts","area":"validation/error scope","issue":"Validation is lazy and the catch-all invalidates unrelated metrics.","evidence":"Orders are validated only if completions and durationMs are non-null; visits only if registrations non-null. Any InvalidMetricFacts (e.g. one bad order) returns invalid for all five metrics, including registration and attendance already computed correctly.","impact":"Corrupt inputs can go unnoticed on some paths, while on others a single bad row discards independent, valid metrics.","recommended_fix":"Validate every non-null collection up front. Scope failures per metric dependency (visits→registration, viewing→attendance/viewing/completion, completions+orders→order).","required_test":"Invalid order with durationMs=null reports invalid_data; invalid order leaves registrationRate and attendanceRate available.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"live-core-metrics-read-model.ts","area":"missing evidence / plausibility","issue":"Segments are not checked for a plausible constant playback rate.","evidence":"Only wallEnd>wallStart, mediaEnd>mediaStart and mediaEnd<=duration are checked. A 1 ms wall segment spanning 100000 ms of media yields full coverage and 1 ms exposure.","impact":"A bad ingestion row can mint completion with negligible exposure; the 'validated by ingestion' claim is unenforced here.","recommended_fix":"Require an adapter-provided rate bound or validated flag (e.g. 0.25x–4x) and fail closed outside it, or document and test the contract.","required_test":"Segment with rate far above the allowed maximum → invalid_data; boundary-rate segment accepted.","confidence":0.5},{"severity":"MINOR","file":"live-core-metrics-read-model.test.ts","area":"test coverage","issue":"Several approved boundaries and claims are untested.","evidence":"'overlapping devices' test only duplicates identical rows, never distinct partially overlapping intervals. No visit-at-S/T or visit==verification tie test (code counts verifiedAt>=visit). Order at T-1 untested. No non-unit-rate T test.","impact":"Regressions in union exposure, V window edges and tie attribution would pass unnoticed.","recommended_fix":"Add tests for each boundary and an overlap-device case with expected union seconds.","required_test":"Two devices overlapping wall 0–60s and 30–90s → 90s; visit at S counted, at T excluded; verification==visit pinned; order at T-1 included.","confidence":0.7}]}
